doc.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012

title: Guitar versus piano and the ease of sounding like a guitarist
summary: Discussion of guitarists and ears, and how guitar replaced the parlor piano as the easy instrument.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: That’s really cool. And I followed a little bit of that path, but I have a feeling that all that, plus with your heavy metal guitar really congealed for you. Because I have this weird thing with guitars. Like guitar players don’t necessarily know what they’re doing. That’s my sense of it. That doesn’t mean they’re not good. I mean I’ve played with some guitar players who if you ask them the chord they’ll show you, “Here’s what it is” and show the hand. Yet their ears are so good I’m jealous.

Oh I understand completely. Guitar is sort of what a piano is about a hundred years ago. A lot of people had access to one. I mean a hundred years ago almost every house, or a lot of houses, had a piano in the parlor, and everybody could read music on it. And today piano is just a large bulky instrument and it’s easier for people to have a guitar and for some reason it seems that they can instantly play music on it in a way that sounds pretty much like what they hear on the radio. In other words, and I don’t want to say that the bar has been lowered that far that you can now play music from the radio — but I guess I am saying that. I mean I can’t help but say it. Because it is easier. You’re playing fewer chords, you’re not reading any notes to play A minor and E minor and G and C, you can pretty much get by with that much, and even less today with the synthesized notes, you just hit a button and it plays for you. But I understand. I understand how you feel about guitar, and I think the same thing sometimes that if you just do some tricks and it sounds © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

very guitaristic, it sounds very familiar. Like, “Okay, that sounds like a great guitar player.” And you can sound like a great guitar player I guess easier than you can sound like a great, great, great piano player.
You follow that line of reasoning?
Especially if you’ve got a fuzz box and you’ve got distortion and all the gizmos and the volume at 100 decibels.
